newsitem.title: PERU: Inflation fight still Venezuela's priority -Casas.
newsitem.headline: Inflation fight still Venezuela's priority -Casas.

text.p: Venezuela continues to set priority on its goal of slashing inflation over other targets such as boosting exports through a competitive exchange rate, Venezuelan Central Bank President Antonio Casas Gonzalez said Wednesday.
"One has to have a predominant goal and ours is to control inflation," Casas told Reuters in an interview during a break from a meeting of central bank officials from the Americas and Spain.
Venezuela's inflation was the highest in the region in 1996 at 103.2 percent and the government has set a target of reducing it to between 30 and 35 percent this year.
Monthly inflation fell to 1.6 percent in March -- its lowest monthly level for five years.

Casas attributed the drop in inflation largely to the stability of the exchange rate since the launching of an economic reform programme in April 1996. Venezuela's exchange rate has remained broadly stable between 470 and 480 bolivars per dollar for over 10 months.

Casas acknowledged that this stability had led to criticisms that the exchange rate was damaging Venezuela's competitiveness but said that a more competitive exchange rate would have to wait until the fight against inflation had been won.

"With inflation rates well below those of recent years it will be much easier to manage the exchange rate situation so that it does not damage the possibility of increasing exports or disproportionately encourage imports," he said.
Casas added, however, that in spite of concerns of exchange rate overvaluation, exports have shown a promising increase in recent months.
Non traditional exports, which exclude oil and iron, were up $87 million, or 14.8 percent, at $681 million in the first two months of 1997, compared to $594 million in the same period last year.
